pullRequest.title: Prepare Build 29 release and preserve backend capacity
pullRequest.body:
Build 29 requires release tooling that preserves the immutable Build 27/28 history while accepting its own deployment, custody and owner-device proofs. Add explicit Build 29 support with the existing source, CI, chronology, byte-hash and exact-artifact checks intact. Recover the original Build 28 construction closure and private-custody proof, and bind the separate Build 29 custody decision.

Resolve the review finding that a coherent historical Build 28 approval/CI tuple could authorize newer source: constrain that historical contract to the actual signed Build 28 ancestry boundary. Preserve the current capacity limit by declaring maxInstances:20 on all 19 Functions. The pinned SDK/CLI previously emitted a null reset for all 19; the new manifests differ only in those cap values. Historical 15-existing/four-new comparison remains historical, and successor control verification must compare all 19 existing services.

Bind Build 29 delegation to immutable intended29, independently selected expected29 and coherent policy, package version and ledger read from the exact source Git commit. The predeployment source may retain Build28 metadata before the final Build29 metadata merge. Actual future/mixed generations and a Build30 candidate cannot reuse the Build29 tuple; historical28 remains separately verifiable.

The owner phone's installed APK exactly matches governed Build 28 and the original signer. The separate additive audit_logs index is now READY, with all 67 source indexes present and the original 66 definitions/identities, eight overrides and active Rules preserved. The owner has confirmed all users are stopped and will wait. Functions/Rules deployment, remote build reservation, signing, installation and distribution remain pending.

Validation:
- Before the final corrections, 118 full authority tests, 53 private-custody tests, 334 completed-custody cases, 910 owner-device policy cases, 31 focused Flutter contracts and full production-policy verification passed. Counts overlap.
- The complete stale Build 28 tuple bypass was reproduced on three actual Git ancestry cases before repair; 19 focused authority tests passed after repair, including unchanged historical deployment evidence and the signed upper boundary.
- 133 source-option, backend-control and historical public-proof tests passed, preserving the historical contracts and rejecting mixed, dynamic and incorrect capacity declarations.
- TypeScript compilation, both deployment inventories, 16 SDK export/identity/security tests, the full production policy and all 150 canonical source-audit checks passed. A fresh-process test verifies workflow-first import order. Actual pinned SDK/CLI reproduction confirms explicit20 on every endpoint.
- All six historical primary files/sidecars and all 18 closure entries independently checked. Diff validation is clean.
- The future-generation bypass was reproduced with a coherent Build30 candidate and an actual Build30 Git source. All 36 focused generation/history cases were validated (34 initial passes and two expectation-only corrections passing on rerun); an additional focused check verifies exact numeric intent and rejects non-commit source references. Full policy and all 150 canonical checks passed, and independent review found no concrete blocker in the generation repair.
- Final-head hosted release/security checks and fresh bot review are required before normal merge. Normal merge preserves the immutable custody anchor commit. Artifact construction remains refused until actual source/backend parity is proved.

head_commit.message:
Merge pull request #376 from abhishekvatsa/codex/build29-release-preparation

Prepare Build 29 release and preserve backend capacity.

Source/preparation merge only. The owner explicitly accepted the exact-head ChatGPT technical assessment as the alternative final review for this PR, recorded in issuecomment-5763473046 and pullrequestreview-5268775631. Final-head release-gate and CodeQL checks passed. Preserve commit/custody ancestry.

No production deployment, build-number reservation, production signing, installation, activation or distribution is authorized by this merge. The resulting main commit requires its own CI and subsequent release gates.
